units.function: Filesystem integration test listing a desired Paperclip skill as missing and persistently installing it as a symbolic link into the Claude/OpenCode shared user skill home.
units.dependencyDirection: Agent/Company adapter configuration supplies HOME and desired skill keys; the OpenCode adapter inspects and mutates HOME/.claude/skills, linking a Paperclip-owned source into a vendor-shared runtime directory.
units.keyDataModels: Agent/company/adapter identity, HOME, desired skill key, persistent mode, warning, missing/installed state and target symlink path.
units.lifecycle: List reports the desired skill missing and warns that OpenCode shares Claude's skill home; sync creates a persistent symlink and reports installed state.
units.testAssessment: The happy path verifies the surprising shared-home destination and actual symlink materialization. Missing are host-owner consent, path/symlink escapes, existing-file conflicts, permissions, concurrent sync, uninstall/rollback/update, immutable version/hash/license/signature, source disappearance, tenant isolation and proof that the runtime loaded the skill.
units.designRationale: Make Paperclip skills visible to OpenCode through the vendor's currently shared Claude-compatible discovery directory without copying contents.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs one vendor-neutral skill/package lifecycle even when different Agent products share or reinterpret persistent host directories.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE only. A Connector-node SkillPackageManager must be the canonical owner of signed install plans, explicit host consent, collision policy, rollback and activation attestations; an OpenCode driver may declare that its target is shared with Claude but must not independently own mutation policy.
units.responsibilityConflict: Caller-controlled HOME is persistently mutated without an accountable host owner, approved package digest, data/tool grant or rollback receipt. A symlink and installed label do not prove authorization for any Work contract.

units.function: Unit tests projecting desired Grok skills as ephemeral workspace-mounted configuration and reporting unavailable desired skills without persistent installation.
units.dependencyDirection: Agent/Company adapter configuration and available runtime skills enter the Grok adapter; it emits a normalized snapshot describing next-run workspace injection rather than mutating a user home.
units.keyDataModels: Agent/company/adapter identity, desired and available skill keys, ephemeral mode, configured/missing state, external_unknown origin, warning and null target path.
units.lifecycle: Available desired skills are marked configured for copying into executionWorkspace/.claude/skills on the next run; unavailable keys remain missing with a warning and no persistent target.
units.testAssessment: The tests distinguish configured ephemeral state from unavailable state and assert no persistent target. Missing are actual next-run injection, cleanup after success/failure/cancel, workspace isolation, traversal/symlink handling, package digest/version/license/signature, duplicate names, size limits, policy denial and runtime activation evidence.
units.designRationale: Fit Grok's runtime skill discovery by staging selected skills per execution instead of installing them into a durable host directory.
units.companyOsProblem: Connector executions need lease-scoped tools that are materialized only for an authorized Work attempt and destroyed with verifiable cleanup.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the ephemeral lifecycle as the preferred enterprise default, but implement it under the canonical Connector-node SkillPackageManager with immutable package identity, Work/data-policy binding, sandboxed materialization, cleanup receipt and runtime attestation.
units.responsibilityConflict: Configured means only that a key is scheduled for copying; it does not prove who approved it, what code digest ran, which data it could access, that cleanup occurred or that the Agent actually loaded it.

units.function: Filesystem tests projecting desired Codex skills for ephemeral next-run injection, proving sync does not persist them into CODEX_HOME and normalizing a legacy flat skill reference.
units.dependencyDirection: Agent/Company adapter configuration supplies CODEX_HOME and desired skill references; the Codex adapter returns canonical configured entries while deferring materialization to an isolated execution home.
units.keyDataModels: Agent/company/adapter identity, CODEX_HOME, canonical repository/name/key, legacy flat key, ephemeral mode and configured state.
units.lifecycle: List marks the canonical skill configured for next-run CODEX_HOME/skills injection; sync leaves the durable configured home untouched; legacy paperclip normalizes to the canonical key.
units.testAssessment: Tests cover non-persistence, configured projection and backward-compatible key normalization. Missing are the materialization/cleanup path, isolated-home ownership, collision and traversal cases, immutable package provenance, policy approval, failed/cancelled run cleanup, version migration and runtime activation proof.
units.designRationale: Avoid polluting a user's durable Codex home by injecting selected skills only into the isolated home prepared for an execution.
units.companyOsProblem: Codex and other Connectors need consistent ephemeral capability leases without vendor-specific state becoming the control plane's source of truth.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT non-persistence and canonical-key migration tests. The Company OS owner remains a vendor-neutral SkillPackageManager and capability lease; Codex-specific code only materializes an approved digest into an isolated runtime and returns activation/cleanup attestations.
units.responsibilityConflict: Configured state lacks responsible-human approval, Work/contract/data scope and executable digest. The test proves absence from one durable path, not destruction of every temporary copy or non-use after lease expiry.
